## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Iran and Oman near deal on Hormuz shipping routes as energy corridor remains US blockade hostage

Iran and Oman have reached agreement on proposed shipping routes and coordinates through the Strait of Hormuz after three weeks of negotiations, with a joint statement moving to final drafting stage as of August 5. The accord covers inbound and outbound commercial passages, a joint coordination center for maritime traffic, and sovereign arrangements between both nations. However, Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi emphasized the strait remains closed: reopening depends entirely on the US removing its naval blockade and halting attacks on Iranian infrastructure in the region.

**Why it matters.** The Strait of Hormuz handles roughly 21% of global oil supply. For Shashank's context—India imports 80% of its crude from Middle Eastern suppliers, with the bulk transiting this chokepoint. A US-blockaded Hormuz directly raises oil prices, strains India's current account and rupee, and forces costlier rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope. This agreement signals Iran and Oman moving toward reopening commerce, but also crystallizes the Trump administration's use of naval coercion as a negotiating tool—a dynamic that shapes geopolitical risk premia across energy markets and India's energy bill. The timing coincides with the separate munitions crisis limiting US strike capacity, suggesting Iran may perceive shifting leverage.

**Action.** Monitor Bloomberg and Reuters for the finalized Iran-Oman joint statement; track Brent crude and USD/INR spreads for market repricing of Hormuz risk. Read the Carnegie Endowment analysis of US naval strategy in the Gulf to understand the blockade mechanics and historical precedent. Conversations with India's crude traders and RBI watchers will clarify real import-cost impacts.

### Trump confronts Hegseth over critical air-defense depletion as Iran war strains US munitions stockpile

At a Camp David meeting on August 5, President Trump clashed sharply with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over severe US munitions shortages, citing depleted interceptor stocks as the reason for holding back additional strikes on Iran. Pentagon data shows the US has consumed approximately 80% of THAAD anti-ballistic interceptors and 50% of Patriot air-defense missiles due to the ongoing Iran conflict. These shortages now constrain Trump's military options and have prompted Gulf allies to voice concerns about their own air-defense readiness against Iranian missile and drone attacks.

**Why it matters.** US military readiness directly shapes the geopolitical risk calculus that affects India. A depleted munitions stockpile signals limits to sustained US military commitments—relevant to Taiwan contingencies, NATO deterrence, and Middle East stability. For India, the immediate risk is Hormuz closure or escalation if the US cannot credibly threaten further strikes; the secondary risk is that munitions constraints push the Trump administration to negotiate with Iran, potentially reshaping Gulf alignments that India depends on for energy and trade. From a quant/prop perspective, this is a volatility inflection point: markets will reprice the probability and severity of Iran escalation, with cascading effects on oil and EM currency carry trades.

**Action.** Read CSIS briefings on US Indo-Pacific munitions stockpile comparisons and production timelines; monitor Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley equity research on defense contractors for clues on rearmament demand. Track CME futures for crude oil vol expansion and INR forwards for India-specific energy-risk repricing over the next 2–4 weeks.

*Sources: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/08/05/trump-hegseth-clashed-camp-david-over-iran-missile-depletion-concerns/) · [cbsnews.com](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-us-munitions-shortages-iran-war/) · [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/6/trump-vows-to-find-leakers-after-reports-of-depleted-iran-war-munitions)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Google DeepMind Restructures as Kavukcuoglu Takes Helm; Hassabis Pivots to Alphabet Chief Scientist

Demis Hassabis stepped down as CEO of Google DeepMind on August 5, 2026, transitioning to chairman and Alphabet chief scientist, while Koray Kavukcuoglu — the lab's CTO and Alphabet's chief AI architect — was elevated to senior vice president overseeing Gemini model development, frontier research, and product teams. The move addresses escalating pressure: Gemini 3.5 Pro has slipped months past its June target, eight senior researchers departed in two months (including Jeff Dean and Google AI colleagues), and both OpenAI and Anthropic have widened their lead in frontier capability benchmarks. Kavukcuoglu brings 13 years at DeepMind, including founding the deep learning team and leading breakthroughs like WaveNet and DQN.

**Why it matters.** This reorganization signals Google's structural execution problems, not just competitive disadvantage. Moving a visionary founder to a long-term AGI strategy role while installing an operations-focused exec to fix Gemini delivery suggests Google's engineering velocity collapsed. For anyone tracking deployment timelines or infrastructure spending, this means DeepMind's next flagship is now under different leadership and timeline pressure — expect either rushed releases or further delays. The broader signal: frontier AI labs are starting to bifurcate founder-scientist and operations-exec roles, acknowledging that scale and speed demand execution discipline separate from research vision.

**Action.** If you're evaluating models for production, deprioritize Gemini 3.5 Pro until it ships and is benchmarked; the delay now exceeds normal iteration cycles. If you track org structure as a leading indicator for capability timelines, flag DeepMind's restructuring as a sign of internal friction on execution. For researchers: Hassabis's pivot to "chief scientist" is worth watching — it may signal a deeper investment in theoretical AGI work at Alphabet level, separate from product.

*Sources: [[Google DeepMind Leadership Changes](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/technology/news/story/google-deepmind-announces-major-leadership-changes-demis-hassabis-steps-down-as-ceo-all-details-547553-2026-08-06)]([Google DeepMind Leadership Changes](https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/technology/news/story/google-deepmind-announces-major-leadership-changes-demis-hassabis-steps-down-as-ceo-all-details-547553-2026-08-06)) · [[Bloomberg Opinion: DeepMind's New AI Boss](https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2026-08-06/google-deepmind-new-ai-boss-has-big-problems-to-fix-after-hassabis-move)]([Bloomberg Opinion: DeepMind's New AI Boss](https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2026-08-06/google-deepmind-new-ai-boss-has-big-problems-to-fix-after-hassabis-move)) · [[Kavukcuoglu Named SVP Google DeepMind](https://aidailypost.com/news/kavukcuoglu-takes-over-google-deepmind)]([Kavukcuoglu Named SVP Google DeepMind](https://aidailypost.com/news/kavukcuoglu-takes-over-google-deepmind))*

### Claude Fable 5 Dominates Coding Benchmarks as Anthropic's Fastest-Ramping Deployment Reaches Peak Benchmark Coverage

Claude Fable 5 leads public benchmark snapshots verified August 6, 2026: 70.5% on CursorBench (coding task completion), 80.3% on SWE-Bench Pro (real-world bug fixes), and 64% on MirrorCode, ahead of GPT-5.6 Sol across all three. The model, released June 9 but constrained by export controls until June 30 global availability, is now the default on Claude Max and Claude Pro. Critically, SWE-bench Verified — which asks models to fix actual bugs in real repositories — has jumped from ~60% across the field to nearly 100% in one year, with frontier systems now reliably automating software engineering tasks at scale.

**Why it matters.** This is not marketing; it's a capability inflection. Coding benchmarks correlate directly with agent autonomy and deployment economics. When a model hits 80%+ on SWE-bench, it means reducing junior-to-mid engineer overhead on codegen and review is no longer a "future promise" — it's a shipping ROI today. For consulting practices and engineering teams building AI-assisted workflows, Fable 5's performance profile (strong on coding, reasoning, and long-context tasks) justifies migrating codegen workloads from smaller models. For infrastructure decisions: if your team is still running o1-preview for agentic code tasks, Fable 5 offers 50-70% cost reduction with similar or better real-world bug-fix performance.

**Action.** Run SWE-Bench Verified against your internal code on both Claude Fable 5 and your current default (likely GPT-5.6 Sol or Claude Opus 5). The benchmark's grounding in actual open-source repos means it predicts real-world performance better than terminal-bench synthetic tasks. For teams using models for code review or generation, test Fable 5 on your own repositories this week — the gap in coding performance justifies a benchmark run before signing next quarter's contract.

## 🇮🇳 India

### RBI Signals Growth Optimism With 6.7% FY27 Forecast, Rates Unchanged at 5.25%

The Reserve Bank of India held its repo rate at 5.25% on August 5, 2026, while raising its full-year GDP growth forecast to 6.7% and cutting inflation outlook to 5.0%. Governor Sanjay Malhotra cited desire for "greater clarity" on inflation before moving rates. The six-member Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to maintain a Neutral stance, signaling the RBI will support economic growth while balancing price pressures.

**Why it matters.** For founders and engineers building in India, this is a green light. Higher GDP growth projections mean stronger consumer demand, corporate profits, and tax revenues—all critical for startup valuations and follow-on funding rounds. Held rates at 5.25% keep borrowing costs stable for bootstrap operations and bridges. The Neutral stance removes rate-hike risk that would have crushed late-stage funding multiples and made rupee debt less attractive. Early-stage teams should expect VC dry powder to remain deployed, and Series B+ rounds to continue.

**Action.** Read the RBI's full monetary policy statement and forward guidance on the official RBI website. Track Q2 FY27 GDP data (due mid-August) to see if growth trajectory holds. Watch for credit growth acceleration in bank earnings reports starting next week—that signals whether liquidity translates to startup capital.

*Sources: [[India Infoline RBI Policy Update](https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/economy/rbi-policy-update-august-2026-repo-rate-unchanged-at-5-25-fy27-gdp-growth-raised-to-6-7-inflation-forecast-cut)]([India Infoline RBI Policy Update](https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/economy/rbi-policy-update-august-2026-repo-rate-unchanged-at-5-25-fy27-gdp-growth-raised-to-6-7-inflation-forecast-cut)) · [[Forbes India RBI MPC Highlights](https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/rbi-mpc-live-updates-august-2026-repo-rate-sanjay-malhotra-policy-announcement-liveblog/2996705/1)]([Forbes India RBI MPC Highlights](https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/rbi-mpc-live-updates-august-2026-repo-rate-sanjay-malhotra-policy-announcement-liveblog/2996705/1)) · [[Upstox RBI Policy Analysis](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/latest-updates/rbi-policy-august-2026-rates-unchanged-at-5-25-inflation-likely-to-peak-at-5-9-in-q3-fy-27-check-key-takeaways/article-198142/)]([Upstox RBI Policy Analysis](https://upstox.com/news/market-news/latest-updates/rbi-policy-august-2026-rates-unchanged-at-5-25-inflation-likely-to-peak-at-5-9-in-q3-fy-27-check-key-takeaways/article-198142/))*

### OfBusiness Revives $800M IPO Plan, Targets Year-End DRHP Filing

OfBusiness, SoftBank's flagship fintech unicorn, is moving toward a public listing with plans to file its DRHP by mid-November 2026, according to reports on August 5. The company is targeting an $800 million IPO that would value the B2B procurement platform at $5–6 billion. FY26 financials show ₹724 crore net profit (up 21% YoY) on ₹20,645 crore revenue, with EBITDA growing 34% to ₹769 crore. Morgan Stanley, Axis Capital, JPMorgan, and Citigroup are advising the listing.

**Why it matters.** OfBusiness's IPO signals investor confidence in Indian fintech and SaaS businesses after a two-year freeze on unicorn exits. For engineers in Hyderabad and Bangalore building B2B fintech, this is proof of concept: the market wants Indian software solving Indian procurement, supply-chain, and credit problems. Strong profitability and revenue scale show the playbook works without venture subsidy. Watch the IPO pricing to gauge what revenue multiples the market assigns to homegrown fintech—this sets expectations for all downstream B2B startups planning exits.

**Action.** Pull OfBusiness's filed financials on MCA portal once DRHP lands in November. Track banker communications and roadshow updates starting November for insights on how investors are valuing B2B fintech multiples. Flag for comparison when other IndiaStack-era startups file (Razorpay, BharatPe, Chime, etc.).

*Sources: [[Inc42 OfBusiness DRHP Filing](https://inc42.com/buzz/ofbusiness-set-to-file-drhp-for-800-mn-ipo-by-mid-november/)]([Inc42 OfBusiness DRHP Filing](https://inc42.com/buzz/ofbusiness-set-to-file-drhp-for-800-mn-ipo-by-mid-november/)) · [[StartupTalky Funding Roundup](https://startuptalky.com/news/daily-indian-funding-roundup-key-news-5-august-2026/)]([StartupTalky Funding Roundup](https://startuptalky.com/news/daily-indian-funding-roundup-key-news-5-august-2026/)) · [[Dailyhunt OfBusiness IPO](https://m.dailyhunt.in/news/india/english/inc42-epaper-inc/ofbusiness+set+to+file+drhp+for+800+mn+ipo+by+midnovember-newsid-n722204165)]([Dailyhunt OfBusiness IPO](https://m.dailyhunt.in/news/india/english/inc42-epaper-inc/ofbusiness+set+to+file+drhp+for+800+mn+ipo+by+midnovember-newsid-n722204165))*

## 📈 Markets

### RBI Pauses as Inflation Risks Rise; Central Banks in Asymmetric Hold on Sticky Crude

The Reserve Bank of India held its policy repo rate at 5.25% on August 5, maintaining neutral stance, as it lifted its FY27 retail inflation forecast to 5.1% from 4.6% citing persistent oil price pressure. Nifty 50 closed August 6 at 24,636 (up 0.05%) while Sensex gained 0.48% to 78,954.76, led by PSU banks but hamstrung by weakness in autos and IT. Brent crude hovered at $83.53/barrel with geopolitical premium building as Hormuz reopening talks inch forward. Gold surged to $4,307/oz—highest since June 17—as investors hedged inflation and rate-hold risks. INR/USD held at 96 as central bank inaction and inflation anxiety offset equity weakness.

**Why it matters.** RBI's inflation revisions signal the central bank sees crude at $80+ as structural, not cyclical. This anchors rate expectations higher for longer—RBI may cut later than markets priced, flattening the yield curve and pressuring growth valuations. For India's AI-infra and capital-goods cohort, this matters: capex cycles turn on real rate expectations. With India's 10Y G-Sec at 6.84% and UST 10Y at 4.67%, the term premium widens on inflation fears specific to energy-dependent India. Global liquidity stays tight; crude near $85 is a hard ceiling for emerging-market policy easing until supply clarity emerges (Hormuz reopening remains uncertain despite headlines).

**Action.** Watch India CPI for July (due August 12) and the flash PMI on August 21—if either rolls over, RBI faces a cut-hold dilemma. Monitor Brent's break above $85; that triggers emergency-reserve talk in New Delhi. US jobless claims (tonight or tomorrow depending on release calendar) and ADP miss yesterday (slower August hiring) could slow Fed dovishness, keeping 10Y UST anchored, which would support INR relative to EM peers but compress RBI's policy room.

*Sources: [[RBI MPC Decision August 5, 2026](https://www.indiatvnews.com/business/news/rbi-mpc-2026-live-updates-governor-sanjay-malhoraj-repo-rate-update-monetary-policy-committee-latest-news-inflation-other-details-2026-08-05-1050383)]([RBI MPC Decision August 5, 2026](https://www.indiatvnews.com/business/news/rbi-mpc-2026-live-updates-governor-sanjay-malhoraj-repo-rate-update-monetary-policy-committee-latest-news-inflation-other-details-2026-08-05-1050383)) · [[Nifty/Sensex Close August 6](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/stock-market-live-aug-6-nse-bse-sensex-today-nifty-gift-nifty-brent-crude-oil-price-q1-result-share-market-today-ipo-gmp-126080600077_1.html)]([Nifty/Sensex Close August 6](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/stock-market-live-aug-6-nse-bse-sensex-today-nifty-gift-nifty-brent-crude-oil-price-q1-result-share-market-today-ipo-gmp-126080600077_1.html)) · [[Gold Surge and Hormuz Reopening](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/investing/article/gold-prices-today-thursday-august-6-2026-gold-prices-surge-as-hormuz-inches-closer-to-reopening-130743281.html)]([Gold Surge and Hormuz Reopening](https://finance.yahoo.com/personal-finance/investing/article/gold-prices-today-thursday-august-6-2026-gold-prices-surge-as-hormuz-inches-closer-to-reopening-130743281.html)) · [[RBI Inflation Forecast](https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/rbi-mpc-live-updates-august-2026-repo-rate-sanjay-malhotra-policy-announcement-liveblog/2996705/1)]([RBI Inflation Forecast](https://www.forbesindia.com/article/news/rbi-mpc-live-updates-august-2026-repo-rate-sanjay-malhotra-policy-announcement-liveblog/2996705/1))*

### Term Premium Blowout: UST 10Y Rallies to 4.67% While India G-Sec Yields Stick, Tightening EM Rate Squeeze

The US 10-Year Treasury yield climbed 6 basis points to 4.67% on August 6, even as the S&P 500 fell 0.17% to 7,723.55 and the Dow dropped 0.85% to 53,885.10. India's 10-year G-Sec held at 6.84%, showing near-zero move despite RBI's hawkish inflation revision, signaling duration sellers have fled and yield compression is stalled. The 183 bps term premium between India 10Y and US 10Y persists—a reflection that markets no longer price meaningful EM policy differentiation on growth or inflation.

**Why it matters.** For quant prop researchers pricing EM carry, this is signal of crowding unwind. Higher UST yields typically attract US capital away from Indian bonds, narrowing carry and forcing Indian yields up to compete—but that's not happening, implying the arb has already broken and domestic demand for G-Sec has weakened. Brent at $83+ keeps inflation hedges expensive for Indian insurers and provident funds (large G-Sec buyers). The sticky yield curve environment makes duration-extension trades risky and favors short-end plays (5Y, 7Y) where RBI patience is priced in.

**Action.** Track the G-Sec auction scheduled later this month; if demand weakens despite RBI hold, that flags early signs of fiscal deterioration or inflation pass-through acceleration. Watch for any RBI OMO (open-market operation) to steepen the curve; a flat curve into September rate decisions would signal confidence is eroding. Cross-asset: monitor if oil dips below $82; that would crack India's inflation case and force G-Sec yields lower, potentially narrowing US-India spreads and offering a short-duration rotation signal.

*Sources: [[US 10Y Treasury Yield August 6](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)]([US 10Y Treasury Yield August 6](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)) · [[India G-Sec Yield Sticky at 6.84%](https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/investment/story/10-year-g-sec-yield-climbs-to-6-85-in-july-heres-what-pushed-bond-yields-higher-547190-2026-08-05)]([India G-Sec Yield Sticky at 6.84%](https://www.businesstoday.in/personal-finance/investment/story/10-year-g-sec-yield-climbs-to-6-85-in-july-heres-what-pushed-bond-yields-higher-547190-2026-08-05)) · [[S&P 500 and Dow Close](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)]([S&P 500 and Dow Close](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html))*

## 🇮🇳 Indian Stocks

### STERLITE TECHNOLOGIES (NSE): +5.0% upper circuit on ₹960-crore telecom capex order

Sterlite Technologies locked in the 5.0% upper circuit at ₹636.20 on August 5, extending into August 6 trading, after securing a multi-year optical fiber cable supply contract worth approximately ₹960 crore (roughly $115 million USD equivalent) from a domestic telecom operator. The contract spans 2027–2029 with renewal options, indicating sustained capex cycles in India's 5G rollout. Volume lifted sharply on the announcement, with traders citing additional tailwinds from speculation around US import curbs on Chinese telecom equipment pushing the stock to circuit limits.

**Why it matters.** Sterlite's order win signals accelerating telecom infrastructure capex in India. For domestic equipment manufacturers and cable suppliers, this order represents validation of the 5G build-out cycle, with read-across benefits to component suppliers and logistics partners. For an AI engineer in Hyderabad watching domestic sectors, this reflects India's digital infrastructure buildout—the same capex spending that supports cloud and data-center buildout driving AI workload growth.

**Action.** Monitor BSE/NSE regulatory filing for full contract terms, duration, and customer identity (typically disclosed post-announcement). Check FY27E capex guidance updates in Q2 earnings (likely August). Watch if other optical fiber suppliers (Birlasoft, ITI Limited) follow on similar order wins. Circuit filters broke; technical resistance now at ₹667 (prior 52-week high). First support at ₹604 (Aug 4 close).

### SBI (NSE): +2.84% on banking sector tailwinds ahead of Q2 results

State Bank of India advanced 2.84% to 3.22% on August 6, hitting ₹1,073.30 during the session, as banking stocks rallied on sector-wide earnings strength and the Reserve Bank of India's neutral policy stance (repo rate held at 5.25%). Life Insurance Corporation reported 23% year-on-year earnings growth the same day, validating financial-sector resilience. SBI's Q2 FY27 results are scheduled for Friday, August 8, with the pre-result rally suggesting investor confidence in credit growth and margin recovery.

**Why it matters.** Banking sector momentum reflects improving credit offtake and deposit flows as RBI maintains accommodative settings. For PSU banks like SBI, the neutral stance removes downside policy risk while earnings growth validates the loan-loss provisioning cycle has normalized. Cross-read to HDFC Bank, ICICI, and Kotak—all flagging Q2 earnings this week—for consolidated financial-sector health. Domestic consumption and capex cycles appear resilient enough to sustain credit growth, a precursor to broader economic stability.

**Action.** Await SBI Q2 results on August 8 for net interest margin trends, slippage ratios, and guidance. Compare against HDFC Bank (Aug 8) and ICICI Bank (Aug 9) for sector-wide NPA and capital-adequacy trends. BSE/NSE will disclose earnings simultaneously on their websites. Watch deposit-growth commentary; if CRR relief or liquidity tightening emerges in forward guidance, re-rate risk. Resistance at ₹1,085; support at ₹1,050.

## 💹 Global Stocks

### PLTR (NASDAQ): +30.2% on record Q2 earnings beat, FY2026 guidance raised to $8.15B–8.16B

Palantir Technologies closed Tuesday, August 5 near $162.00, up 30% in its strongest one-day move in over two years. The company reported Q2 FY2026 EPS of $0.41—24% ahead of consensus $0.33—on revenue of $1.94 billion, up 93% year-over-year. Management raised full-year 2026 guidance by $500 million at the midpoint, to $8.15–8.16 billion from prior $7.65–7.66 billion, signaling broad AI monetization acceleration beyond infrastructure buildout.

**Why it matters.** Palantir's jump marks a watershed moment for the AI narrative: the Street is now crediting software companies, not just chip suppliers, with capturing secular AI tailwinds. U.S. commercial revenue more than doubled 149% year-over-year to $764 million; remaining deal value hit $6.24 billion. For Indian tech services plays, this validates that AI adoption is broadening into enterprise workflows—a read-across to Accenture, HCLTech, and TCS margin expansion bets. The relative outperformance of AI software over semiconductor mega-caps in a single trading session also suggests money may be rotating from infrastructure plays into applications.

**Action.** Review the full earnings transcript and 10-Q filing (due within 60 days per SEC rules) for visibility on remaining deal value conversion and gross margin profile. PLTR closed Tuesday within 3% of its 52-week high; watch $155–150 as support if the broader market corrects. Key level to monitor: whether commercial deal flow remains >$3.4B annually as guided for 2026.

*Sources: [[Palantir Q2 2026 Earnings Report](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/03/palantir-pltr-earnings-q2-2026.html)]([Palantir Q2 2026 Earnings Report](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/03/palantir-pltr-earnings-q2-2026.html)) · [[Palantir Stock Trading Analysis](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262080546-palantir-pltr-stock-surges-after-q2-earnings-ai-demand-guidance-tradingkey)]([Palantir Stock Trading Analysis](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262080546-palantir-pltr-stock-surges-after-q2-earnings-ai-demand-guidance-tradingkey)) · [[Palantir Investor Relations](https://investors.palantir.com)]([Palantir Investor Relations](https://investors.palantir.com))*

### AVGO (NASDAQ): +6.1% on Palantir tailwinds; semiconductor cycle broadens as AI monetization moves upstream

Broadcom shares rallied 6.1% to $417.80 on Tuesday, August 5, rebounding from a 2% drop two days prior when Goldman Sachs removed it from its U.S. Conviction List. The recovery was fueled by broad-based relief across the semiconductor complex following Palantir's blowout earnings, which suggested AI adoption is accelerating into enterprise deployment rather than stalling on infrastructure. Shares of NVIDIA, AMD, Marvell, and Micron also moved higher alongside AVGO.

**Why it matters.** Broadcom's removal from Goldman's top-picks list on August 3 reflected thesis that "AI monetization" (software, SaaS, cloud services) is now outpacing pure "infrastructure buildout" (GPUs, chip equipment). ### AI algorithm flags dementia risk by analyzing how fast your brain ages during sleep

UC San Francisco and Beth Israel Deaconess researchers developed a machine-learning model that analyzes EEG microstructures during sleep—sleep spindles, slow-wave patterns, and other electrical signatures—to predict dementia risk years before symptoms. Meta-analysis of 7,105 adults from five long-running U.S. community studies showed participants whose brains appeared older than their chronological age on the "Brain Age Index" had significantly elevated dementia risk during follow-up. Results published in npj Aging (Nature Publishing Group) in July 2026.

**Why it matters.** This is a low-cost, potentially at-home-compatible screening tool that detects neurodegeneration earlier and cheaper than blood biomarkers alone. The methodology is immediately actionable: existing wearable sleep trackers and hospital EEG systems can integrate this analysis. For AI-in-health builders, this validates EEG microstructure modeling as a commercial diagnostic modality and demonstrates a path to scaling early cognitive decline detection through sleep monitoring platforms.

**Action.** Read the npj Aging paper for model architecture and EEG feature specs. Clinical teams should pilot Brain Age Index screening in populations with cognitive complaints or dementia family history. Startups should partner with sleep-tracking companies or hospital EEG vendors for wearable/clinical integration. Diagnostic companies should consider this as an add-on module to existing sleep medicine workflows.
